correctness.rationale: Local constancy forces the identity isotropy singleton to be open, hence the unit to be isolated; conversely isolation makes every source-fibre singleton compact-open. The corner and source-fibre calculations then give e_x A e_x ≅ R[G_x] and a free right-isotropy module A e_x. Concrete two-loop and disconnected one-loop examples independently verify the two obstructions.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Existing Steinberg literature is credited for source-fibre isotropy induction. Targeted searches did not locate a prior notice that Proposition 4.1 of arXiv:2609.20230v1 fails at nonisolated paths, nor the combined isolated-unit and unital-corner correction. The elementary criterion may be implicit in older literature, so the novelty claim is deliberately narrow.

value.rationale: The result corrects the foundational embedding used by a recent KP-algebra restriction framework, gives an exact boundary rather than only a counterexample, identifies a second unital-module defect, and supplies the correct corner adjunction while preserving the established general isotropy-induction mechanism.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
